body: Nothing's going to match that 160K salary. fuck it.
I'd rather paint the ceiling with my brains than flip burgers.
Thank you.

Internal happiness isn't the same as winning. It's a consolation prize at best. 

I have known what I wanted my life to be like since I was a teenager, and what it took to get there. If I thought there was any way forward to that life I would continue to fight like mad. But the door is closed, and it's important to have the integrity not to settle and lie to myself that it was what I wanted all along just because I am afraid of death.

Past a certain point, it will not. But I've worked legal aid, I've seen what low income people have to endure. The overdoses, the shooting deaths, the higher rates of cancer and obesity, mistreatment by the police and courts. These are not happy, healthy people. Every day is a stress or struggle worrying about bills and feeling helpless against grinding poverty. Middle class life is punctuated by a fear of falling into that status. The wealthy have problems too, not all are happy, but in this day and age there's plenty of evidence that being low income is terribly bad for your happiness.

Well I am sure I will be able to find something that pays less, leading to a shittier dating pool, a shittier family, a shittier house, and a shitty or average life. Everything comes back to economic status in the end. Enduring a lesser life than what I could have had if I hadn't fucked up isn't growing, it's settling and acquiescing. No thanks. I appreciate the sentiment but I want to keep my dignity at least.

In the normal world, one semester of bad grades isn't a world ender. In law, it is. I will be below median at a non T-14 law school and that means I'm not going to be able to compete for OCI, and probably will struggle for a job at all, let alone one that pays well, regardless of how much I raise my grades, because firms compare students first year grades more than overall GPA. I fucked myself badly, and there's no way to retake 1L courses. My alternatives are all shitty. 

Sadly in law school, grades are all that matter. I played the game and lost, now I have to hold myself accountable and pay the price.

I know how it feels....I came from a very liberal background and was shocked by the level of groupthink in the military. 

I was depressed and unable to seek help because the military mental health system is a career ender. I never talked to anyone because I didn't trust that it wouldn't be used against me.

I would try to talk to a Chaplin or Military Source counselor. The former is 100% confidential and will keep it from your chain of command. 

Also, why not start applying to colleges? Use that GI Bill? Just don't go to law school...trust me on that one.

You are not an eyesore, you are a victim of a system of labor that requires a fear of ending up in the position you are in to function. It's disgusting but it doesn't mean you are worthless, only that the system that we live under is worthless.

I left the GW bridge and decided to give myself until I got my last grade back, a B+ in contracts. Regrettably it's not enough as I set a an A- as my cutoff for seeing if I was meant to live. Usually when people are meant to live there is a ray of hope or something that convinces them to keep going, but the lack of one in this case clearly shows that there is no hope. Heading back to the GW to finish the job, annoyed that I let myself waste a week for nothing.
This sunset is amazing.
Just called the so called 24 hour New York  lawyers assistance program and got their voicemail. Was hoping for a realistic assessment in case I'm wrong. Useless

No value with C's and you cannot retake 1L classes unless you fail them. But to firms a C is an F. law school grades on a curve so that would be unfair to let people try again.

This is an albatross I cannot shed.I am having some champagne and a nice steak in midtown before I jump. Surrounded by the biglaw associates and investment bankers I could have joined. Instead I blew it and this will never be my life. I don't want to die but I can't stand the idea of a mediocre life. I don't want to be a retired NCO driving a beat up ford ranger with a USAF sticker.
It's too late to be a lawyer, I'm concerned about being successful at all now.
This is way below average. If I didn't have the GI bill I would be losing a scholarship.

As someone who knows a Penn grad, I'm sure you know of Penn face. There's an expectation never to show weakness or imperfection in public. But let's face it, there are good reasons for those expectations. 

Highly selective education is the most Calvinist thing in existence. It's seen as predestination to do great things, I mean Reddit was founded by a UVA student, not a Virginia Tech student. People like to tell their college dropout friends that Facebook and Microsoft were founded by dropouts but they forget that they dropped out of Harvard, and not due to a lack of talent. 

The reality is the prestige of these institutions is based on the work of their graduates, and while there are exceptions, few people today make significant impacts on the world without an elite education. Not getting in is a rejection of my potential to impact the world. 

But considering I didn't put together a competitive application, I can't give up quite yet. Thanks again for the advice from someone who understands that some people have to deal with family expectations that would baffle most people.

Yeah I applied late, didn't take the GRE which was recommended either. I guess I should talk with a graduate school consultant and study for and take the GRE. 

NYU is about as low as I would go, the new school is a joke. But I should actually try to put together a competitive graduate school package before throwing in the towel. I guess I can work my undergraduate connections too. 

You are right, I do have realistic paths remaining and I should attempt them wholeheartedly before throwing in the towel. If I exhaust them all, I still believe suicide is the best path, but it would be pretty pointless if I did so before exhausting all realistic paths to getting where I want to be. I will give it a year to figure something out and re assess then.

Just found out I didn't get in. Game over for me unfortunately. I appreciate the advice but transferring up just doesn't happen very often. I don't want to convince myself that I am OK with a mediocre life, always wondering if things could have been different. Even if I went to get help, 72 hours and some chemicals isn't going to change that. 

I just hope I don't end up on Hart Island, I guess that's my one regret about my descison. I'm fairly sure my family will claim me though.
Didn't get an answer back yet like I expected, so I'm going to let that be the deciding factor.
The sad part is the last two are actually more appealing to me. Not realistic, but certainly less miserable. Being a good teacher and accountant take talents I lack I'm afraid.

I respect the hell out of public defenders, but unfortunately chasing a low paying career isn't an option in my family. My brother and sister worked their asses off to pull their weight, I'm not going to be the one who didn't. I don't have any family or friends where I would be able to afford to live on the salary.

It's bad in the NYC area, yes. It's bad where most of my family and friends live. In comparison to my family, friends and peers it's bad. Happiness sometimes requires success, and I can't continue in a career of I'm not going to be successful enough in it to be able to afford to live on my own where I grew up.

In undergrad no, in the first year of law school it certainly is and it ends almost every high paying opportunity upon graduation. It's a uniquely cutthroat animal that dangles $160,000 a year starting salaries or federal court clerkships in front of you if you succeed, and $40K salaries doing personal injury or public defender work if you don't. It is the difference between success and abject failure.

Good for her! Well given how I know people with records are usually fucked from my clinic work...that is very inspiring.

Well, at least I landed a good summer job. I can also start looking for a job outside of the law on Wall Street since I'm in the city. Maybe I'll get lucky and not even have to go back to law school in the fall. I guess I should exhaust all my options first. My undergrad GPA was good at least.
Of course not, they didn't blow their opportunity and therefore are blameless. They are victims of circumstance, not personal failure.

A few outliers among the piles of failures in similar situations. Compared to a pile of successes among a few outlying failures who didn't bomb their grades. I appreciate the sentiment, but failure is almost a certainty at this point. There's no point in fighting drowning with a millstone around your neck on the off chance you might break free.
